lines.caption: This is a tour of pull request 46, which makes CI review an upstream release merge by the fork's own changes only.
It has three parts: what this PR adds, how it was built and verified, and what comes later.
Part 1. What this PR adds.
First, the planner looks for a merge titled Merge upstream thunar, whose tag is not on main yet.
For such a PR, the review suggests changes by default, so it never commits edits to upstream's code.
A push that changes only explainers, or nothing, is skipped, even with a trailer.
The review reads only the fork's side: the conflict resolutions and the commits after the merge.
Inline suggestions can land only on lines the fork itself changed.
And the watcher's skill drops its trailer and Review-accept rules.
lines.say: And the watcher's skill drops its trailer and review accept rules.

lines.caption: Before, CI reviewed every upstream commit in a release, and could even commit edits to upstream's code.
What the fork decides is small, and git's remerge diff shows exactly how each conflict was resolved.
The step list below the diagram explains the same six steps in more detail.
Upstream's own commits are now left out of the review.
Conflict resolutions, even a hand edit hidden in the merge commit, are now reviewed on their own.
Commits after the merge are still reviewed, and the default mode is now suggest.
The PR changes the review script and the watcher's skill, plus this page and its narration.
Part 2. How it was built and verified.
The old planner ran beside the new one on every test branch.
The test branches merged a fake release made by the watcher's own test tool.
A release merge planned as suggest mode, and its diff went from three files to the fork's one.
With a conflict, the diff held the resolution and a hidden edit, but not upstream's change.
An explainer-only push on the release branch was skipped, where the old planner reviewed it again.
When main was merged into the release branch later, the diff still held only the fork's change.
When a revert emptied the fork's side, open findings were still re-checked, and with none the push was skipped.
A normal feature branch planned exactly as before in all four cases tried.
Inline comment lines stayed the same for normal PRs, and only the fork's for a release.
A real review of a release PR was not run here, because it needs CI.
A fresh review agent ran the new functions on a scratch repo and found two medium issues and four low ones.
Both medium ones were fixed: a later merge of main, and how the review skill reads the diff.
The four low ones were left as they are.
The first real check comes with the next release PR, or a watcher test run, after the merge.
The PR, and where the problem was found, are linked here.
Part 3. What comes later.
This PR builds the fork-side review.
You can try it with a watcher test run.
Then the next real release PR is reviewed by the fork's side only.
The watcher keeps the merge's title, and CI does the rest.
In short: a release PR is now reviewed for what the fork changed, not for what upstream released.
